title: Quantum-circuit simulation of three-flavor neutrino oscillations: vacuum, matter, and CP diagnostics
abstract: We simulate three-flavor neutrino oscillations on two-qubit quantum circuits. The flavor space is embedded as $\ket{00}=ν_e$, $\ket{01}=ν_μ$, $\ket{10}=ν_τ$ with the $\ket{11}$ channel kept inert, and the input mixing parameters (NuFIT~5.3, normal ordering) follow the global fit. We verify three physical settings against analytic or exact references: vacuum propagation, reproduced by a mass-eigenstate phase circuit to $\sim 10^{-16}$; constant-density Mikheev--Smirnov--Wolfenstein (MSW) matter effects, showing resonant flavor conversion when the matter potential $A$ crosses $Δm^2_{31}$; and varying-density (supernova shock-shell) propagation by slicing plus second-order Suzuki--Trotter splitting, agreeing with exact evolution to $\sim 10^{-6}$. We report a Suzuki--Trotter precision--resource calibration varying order, step number, and matrix/probability error. It delimits brute-force Trotterization on solar baselines: we quantify both standard alternatives, coherence averaging and adiabatic MSW. We also compute quantum-information diagnostics from the same model parameters, namely mode entanglement and the CP asymmetry. Finally, we extend the framework to open quantum systems via a Lindblad master equation with dephasing and absorptive channels. These results provide a reproducible link between low-energy oscillation observables and quantum-information measures.
summary: This work develops a quantum circuit simulation framework to model three-flavor neutrino oscillations under various physical conditions, including vacuum, matter effects, and decoherence. It rigorously verifies the simulation against known analytical results while also calculating quantum information diagnostics like entanglement and CP asymmetry. The paper establishes a reproducible quantum pipeline connecting particle physics observables to quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper simulates three-flavor neutrino oscillations across various astrophysical environments (vacuum, matter, supernova) using quantum circuits.
main_result: The quantum circuit framework successfully reproduces analytical results for oscillation probabilities and establishes a quantitative link between low-energy oscillation observables and quantum-information measures like mode entanglement and CP asymmetry.
method: The evolution is simulated by encoding the flavor space into a two-qubit system and applying time evolution via quantum circuits, utilizing Suzuki-Trotter splitting for time discretization.
model_or_system: The system is three-flavor neutrino oscillation governed by a Hamiltonian that includes vacuum terms and density-dependent matter potentials. The simulation is extended to open quantum systems using a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Oscillation probabilities ($P_{\alpha	o eta}$), mode entanglement (Concurrence), and CP asymmetry ($\Delta P$).
important_parameters: NuFIT 5.3 parameters, matter potential $A(r)$, and simulation parameters like Trotter order and step number.

figures_summary: Figures illustrate the successful reproduction of vacuum oscillation results to high precision, the resonance behavior in MSW matter, and the convergence rates of the Trotter approximation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically verifies the simulation across three regimes: vacuum propagation, constant-density MSW matter, and varying-density supernova shock-shell propagation. It then extends the model to include quantum information diagnostics and open-system decoherence.
why_interesting: The explicit use of quantum circuits to model fundamental particle physics processes, combined with the calculation of quantum information measures, provides a novel computational bridge between particle physics phenomenology and quantum information theory.
